gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker Prime 100W 3-port (A2688), which ChatGPT showed at $69.99, is sold out on Anker's US store as of 2026-11-17, along with its 3-port 100W sibling (A121B). Anker's in-stock 100W chargers there have one port each (Nano 100W A2679 at $35.99, Laptop Charger Pro A120F at $49.99), and its in-stock 3-port Nano 70W (B121A, $39.99) gives the laptop only 45 W when a second USB-C device is plugged in.
standout_why: ChatGPT cited no page. All 12 results were anker.com pages (the A120F, A2688 and A121B product pages, the 100W and laptop collections, and an Anker blog post). Each one covers a single Anker model or lists Anker models without per-port splits. None compares prices across brands, none says that both of Anker's 3-port 100W models are sold out while the in-stock 100W models have one port, and none shows the 45 W + 22.5 W split on the in-stock 3-port model. ChatGPT's answer still shows A2688 at $69.99 as if it can be bought.
decides: ChatGPT's multi-device pick (Anker Prime 100W, $69.99) can't be bought from Anker US today, so a shopper who wants a laptop and a phone on one brick needs a different pick. Anker's in-stock options are either one-port 100W bricks ($35.99 to $49.99) or the $39.99 Nano 70W 3-port, which drops the laptop to 45 W when two USB-C devices share it. The next Anker 3-port step that is in stock is the Prime 160W (A2687) at $115.99. That leaves room for our UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-port as the in-stock multi-port 100W pick, but its price has to be re-read today. Our page's Anker row ('See maker page; sold on Amazon') should say the charger is sold out at Anker US. Separately, the cells in our current page's JSON are shifted by one column: 'model' holds the wattage and 'ports' holds the price.
